intro: Judgements and possibility take the subjunctive; affirmative certainty takes the indicative.
p.es importante que.consejo: It is a judgement: the next verb goes in the subjunctive. With no subject, use the infinitive: «es importante reciclar».
p.es necesario que.consejo: Always subjunctive if you name who acts: «es necesario que todos reciclemos».
p.es normal que.consejo: Even if the fact is real, the judgement asks for the subjunctive: «es normal que esté cansado».
p.es posible que.consejo: Possibility is not certainty, so it goes with the subjunctive: «es posible que llueva».
p.es una pena que.consejo: It expresses regret. With «una» in front: «es una pena que no vengas».
p.está bien que.consejo: It approves something. The opposite is «está mal que». Both ask for the subjunctive.
p.es verdad que.consejo: It presents something as real, so it goes with the indicative: «es verdad que tienes razón».
p.está claro que.consejo: Affirmative certainty: indicative. If you negate («no está claro que»), you move to the subjunctive.
p.es evidente que.consejo: It is spelled with «v»: «e-bi-DEN-te». It goes with the indicative.
p.no es verdad que.consejo: When you deny the truth, you use the subjunctive: «no es verdad que sea tarde».
p.reciclar.consejo: It has a soft «c»: «re-thi-KLAR». The subjunctive, «reciclemos», keeps the same sound.
p.plástico.consejo: It has an accent on the «á»: «PLAS-ti-ko». It is masculine: «el plástico».
b1.texto:
Expressions that **judge** a situation or speak of **necessity** and **possibility** take the **subjunctive** in the «que» part:

- **Es importante que** reciclemos.
- **Es normal que** estés cansado.
- **Es posible que** llueva.
- **Está bien que** lo digas.

Expressions that present something as **certain** take the **indicative**:

- **Es verdad que** tiene razón.
- **Está claro que** no viene.

If you **deny** the certainty, you go back to the subjunctive: **no es verdad que tenga** razón.

If the sentence is general and names nobody, use the infinitive: **es importante reciclar**.
b2.f0.texto: It is obvious that we use too much plastic.
b2.f1.texto: And it is necessary for all of us to recycle.
b2.f2.texto: It is normal for people to be worried.
b2.f3.texto: But it is not true that we cannot do anything.
b2.f4.texto: It is clear that you are right.
b2.f5.texto: It is important to start today.
b2.f6.texto: It is good that each person brings their own bag.
b2.f7.texto: It is a pity that there is so much rubbish in the sea.
b4.texto:
Look at the three groups:

- **Judgement** → subjunctive: es importante que · es necesario que · es normal que · está bien que · es una pena que · me parece mal que.
- **Possibility** → subjunctive: es posible que · es probable que · puede que.
- **Certainty** → indicative: es verdad que · es cierto que · está claro que · es evidente que · es obvio que.

If you **deny** certainty, the mood changes: **no es verdad que** tenga razón · **no está claro que** venga.

For a general idea, naming nobody, use the **infinitive**: es importante **dormir** bien · es necesario **reciclar**.
b4.e0.texto: It is important that we recycle plastic.
b4.e1.texto: It is true that you are right.
b4.e2.texto: It is not clear that he will come.
b5.f0.texto: The beach wakes up with a fresh smell of salt and seaweed.
b5.f1.texto: The grey waves arrive slowly and leave white lace on the sand.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía walks barefoot along the shore with a bucket in her hand.
b5.f3.texto: The cold water wets her ankles and pulls a little cry from her.
b5.f4.texto: A lonely seagull flies in circles over the dark rocks.
b5.f5.texto: Among the seaweed shines a half-buried plastic bottle.
b5.f6.texto: Pablo picks it up carefully and puts it in the bucket.
b5.f7.texto: Further on there is a broken net and a shoe without laces.
b5.f8.texto: The two of them walk along the shore with an attentive gaze.
b5.f9.texto: At the end of the walk, the sand shines clean under the afternoon sun.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! The judgement asks for the subjunctive: reciclemos.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Reciclamos» is indicative; here you need the subjunctive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not follow «que» with a subject.
b6.pregunta: It is a judgement with the subject «todos». What is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Possibility is not certainty: it asks for the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes! It presents something as certain: indicative.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is a judgement: it asks for the subjunctive.
b7.pregunta: Which expression asks for the indicative?
b8.o0.refuerzo: «Tengas» is subjunctive; with certainty comes the indicative.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Está claro que» states: indicative.
b8.o2.refuerzo: After «que» you need a conjugated verb.
b8.pregunta: The sentence presents something as certain. What is missing?
b9.frase: Es normal que la gente esté preocupada
b9.traduccion: It is normal for people to be worried
b10.o0.refuerzo: That's it! When you deny the truth, doubt appears: subjunctive.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The indicative is for stating certainty, not for denying it.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive is not used after «que».
b10.pregunta: You deny a certainty: «no es verdad que…». Which mood follows?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «It is important to recycle».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Tiene» is indicative; after «no es verdad que» comes the subjunctive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Tendrá» is future; here you need the present subjunctive.
b12.pregunta: You deny that he is right. What is missing?
p.reciclemos.consejo: From «reciclar». The «-emos» ending is subjunctive, used to suggest doing something together.
p.preocupada.consejo: From «preocuparse». The «-a» ending agrees with a woman or a feminine noun.
p.podamos.consejo: From «poder». In the subjunctive it keeps the stem and takes the -amos ending.
p.algas.consejo: Plants that grow in the sea. «Alga» is one plant; the final -s makes it plural.
p.dejan.consejo: From «dejar». It can mean to leave something behind. The «j» sounds like «h».
p.encaje.consejo: A delicate fabric full of holes and patterns. The «j» sounds like «h».
p.moja.consejo: From «mojar». The «j» sounds like «h». Here the water wets her feet.
p.tobillos.consejo: Where the foot meets the leg. «ll» sounds like «y», so say «to-BI-yos».
p.arranca.consejo: From «arrancar», to pull out with force. The «rr» at the start is strong.
p.grito.consejo: A sudden sound from the throat. It comes from «gritar», to shout.
p.gaviota.consejo: A white and grey sea bird. The Spanish «v» is pronounced like «b».
p.solitaria.consejo: From «solo», alone. The unstressed «ia» sounds like «ya».
p.vuela.consejo: From «volar». The «v» sounds like «b», and «ue» is one syllable.
p.rocas.consejo: Large stones on the coast. The «c» before «a» sounds like «k».
p.enterrada.consejo: From «enterrar», to bury. It describes a feminine noun like «botella».
p.red.consejo: Ropes or threads knotted with holes, used to catch fish. It is short: «RED».
p.rota.consejo: From «romper», to break. It agrees with «red», which is feminine.
p.zapato.consejo: What you wear on your foot. The «z» sounds like «th».
p.cordones.consejo: The strings you tie on your shoes. It is plural, so it ends in -es.
p.recorren.consejo: From «recorrer», to go across or along. The «rr» sounds strong: «re-KO-rren».
p.mirada.consejo: From «mirar», to look. Think of the eyes at work when you see «mirada».
p.atenta.consejo: It agrees with «mirada», which is feminine, so it ends in -a.
